paper_title: PC2P: Multi-Agent Path Finding via Personalized-Enhanced Communication and Crowd Perception
summary:
PC2P: Multi-Agent Path Finding via Personalized-Enhanced Communication and Crowd Perception - Guotao Li, Shaoyun Xu, Yuexing Hao, Yang Wang, Yuhui Sun, 2026

Li, Xu, Hao, Wang, and Sun target decentralized multi-agent path finding under partial observability, where MARL-based planners must coordinate in real time without centralized search but degrade sharply in dense scenes because communication is indiscriminate, local observations underrepresent congestion structure, and deadlocks in narrow regions are not explicitly resolved. PC2P is built on a Q-learning-based distributed MAPF framework and introduces a personalized-enhanced communication mechanism over a dynamic interaction graph to answer both which neighbors should communicate and what information should be exchanged. The communication pipeline is organized into three stages, selection, generation, and aggregation, so that each agent first identifies relevant peers under the current graph topology, then forms personalized messages, and finally fuses them for action-value estimation. In parallel, the method augments standard local observations with crowd perception that encodes both static spatial constraints and dynamic occupancy changes, giving the policy a stronger heuristic signal about local congestion and feasible motion structure. These components are coupled with a region-based deadlock-breaking module that invokes expert-guided coordination when agents enter confined areas with extreme blocking patterns, rather than relying on the learned policy alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03301?utm_source=openai))

What is concretely demonstrated is a distributed MAPF system that combines adaptive graph-based communication, congestion-aware perceptual augmentation, and explicit deadlock intervention within a single learned planner, and the reported evaluation claims superiority over prior state-of-the-art distributed MAPF baselines across varied environments. The available web-accessible abstract does not expose the paper’s exact benchmark suite, numerical success-rate improvements, throughput values, or ablation percentages, but it does state that ablation experiments isolate each of the three modules and confirm that personalized communication, local crowd perception, and region-based deadlock resolution each contribute materially to overall performance. The technical contribution is therefore not merely a new message-passing block; it is a decomposition of decentralized MAPF failure modes into communication relevance, congestion observability, and pathological deadlock handling, with a corresponding three-part architecture designed to improve scalability and coordination robustness across heterogeneous environment conditions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03301?utm_source=openai))
